memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "When the child grew older, she took him to Pharaoh's daughter and he became her son. She named him Moses, saying, "I drew him out of the water."" - Exodus 2:10 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The name Moses carries his whole story: drawn out of the water. Every time someone called his name for the next eighty years, they were unknowingly announcing that God rescues.

Then comes the hardest sentence in the verse — she took him to Pharaoh's daughter. A second letting go, this time permanent. She had raised him, taught him, loved him, and now she handed him over to be raised in the house of the man who wanted him dead.

She never lived to see the exodus. She never knew what her son would become. She simply obeyed in the dark.

Much of our faithfulness is like that. We plant, we teach, we pray, and we may never see the harvest. Hebrews says many died in faith without receiving what was promised (Heb 11:13), and God was not ashamed to be called their God.

The child drawn out of the water would one day lead a nation through water. And a greater Deliverer would one day draw us out of far deeper depths.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Am I willing to be faithful even if I never see the outcome?
2. What has God drawn me out of that I should thank Him for today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, You are the God who draws people out. Thank You for rescuing me, and help me to serve faithfully even without seeing the end. Amen.
